method: The sample contains selected policy turning points, market-stress episodes and speeches in the Fed and ECB archives. Coverage depends on recoverable publisher pages. These frequencies describe this set of reports.

The sample accepts original editorial headlines published by Bloomberg, The Wall Street Journal, Financial Times and Reuters on their own websites. Each link identifies the publisher’s article. Editorial tags use only the publicly visible headline.

The action tag describes the meeting step stated or anticipated in the headline. The path tag requires explicit language about future policy. A level is a future direction, a revision compares it with an earlier expected path, and an open path records conditional language or a possible pause. An absent path is unscored.

A market tag records an asset or market direction described by the headline. The separate event-study numbers measure market prices around the central-bank communication. Additional news, publication lags and overlapping releases affect comparisons.

Article timestamps describe pages whose titles can change. The initial timestamp of a later-edited article cannot timestamp its final title. Live-entry timestamps apply to the linked dispatch. Updated times are provided where available. Preview identifies the subject of the text, without certifying the observed title as real-time input.
The downloadable records contain editorial paraphrases, source links and a fingerprint of the reviewed headline. A missing observation means coverage has yet to be verified.
